page_placements.theme: Training origins: harm discrimination predates alignment; post-training creates or amplifies a refusal gate shaped by the objective

record.tranche_reason: The study uses EP-region spans rather than the original difference-in-means direction, and intervenes on harmful-request compliance to test the causal role of refusal-related activations.
record.gate_note: The refusal-related results are EP-region measurements, cross-model region matching, and span interventions. The paper does not report the original difference-in-means direction, adding it to harmless prompts, ablating it at every layer and position, or testing general capability preservation. Values used only to select layers or regions are not separate results. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section 4 uses a different method (unsupervised EP region means, a multi-direction span swap at one layer) on refusal. The swap-versus-projection controls bear on whether refusal is affine and multi-directional (V4). Compliant prompts staying in harmful regions bear on harm being encoded separately from refusal (V5). The paper never builds the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, never ablates at all layers, and never adds a direction to induce refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that instruction tuning reorganises harmful-prompt activations similarly in Gemma and Llama but at different granularities. They find harmfulness stays represented when refusal fails, so failures occur downstream of the harm representation. An L14 harmful-to-benign span swap makes both models comply (0.88/0.91), while projection alone gives 0.00 in Gemma and 0.34 in Llama. They add that separation quality does not predict where the intervention works.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unsupervised EP region means and a multi-direction span swap at selected layers, not a single harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction projected out at every layer and position. The evaluated prompts were excluded from region means but remained in calibration, clustering, and region selection.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention effect varied substantially by layer: L14 was strongest in both models, while other tested layers produced lower compliance; Llama L31 had mostly empty generations. Harmful-region coverage also varied by layer and model.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction tuning sharply increases unsupervised clustering of harmful prompts into wholly harmful regions. Base: 2–23% (Gemma) and up to 53% (Llama). Tuned: 99–100% at the best layers. The gap persists at matched K, and a TF-IDF baseline reaches only 27%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction tuning reorganises harmful-prompt activations into separable regions that base models lack.

fits_no_version.finding: Round-trip correspondence of harmful EP regions between Gemma and Llama rises from 19% (base) to 44% (tuned), and to 68% at the best-separated layers (25/37 vs a permutation-null max of 11). All-region correspondence stays flat (34.5% to 32.4%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-prompt representational structure converges across model families after instruction tuning.

record.problems: The causal intervention evaluates 32 harmful prompts per layer with one model judge. The authors note borderline judgments could move rates by a few prompts, only four layers per model were tested, and the test is not fully unseen because calibration, clustering, and region selection still use the full construction corpus. The random-direction control is limited because it does not match the amount removed from activations. No general-capability preservation test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant refusal or transfer result omitted. Unrelated AxBench concept detection, Taboo secret-word results, SAEBench results, and general EP stability and efficiency results are not about the claim's refusal mechanism.

untested.parts: Not tested: the difference-in-means direction, ablation at every layer and position, adding the direction to induce refusal, and capability preservation. The single-layer span projection (r9, r10) is a different operation.
No comparison of the span against a single difference-in-means direction. No test of cone geometry. Only four layers per model, 32 prompts, one judge.
Harmfulness is inferred from unsupervised region membership by dataset label, not from a probe of the model's own harm judgment. No intervention separating harm from refusal.
No test of transferring a refusal direction across languages, variants or base-to-instruct. Cross-family region correspondence is recorded under fits_no_version.
No test of whether a removable refusal direction exists under different training regimes. Base and instruct models are compared only by clustering.

missing.what: Permutation null for the cross-model round trip: 25/37 matches against a null mean of 2.89 and max of 11. Matched-K and TF-IDF controls for harmful clustering (27.0%).
Label-shuffle null for base-model separation: shuffling labels drops coverage 'to almost nothing'.

record.verdict_notes: The record over-linked rows. V1 rows r9/r10 use a single-layer, multi-direction span projection, so the 'challenges V1' label is unwarranted. V6/V7 rows measure region clustering and cross-family correspondence, not refusal-direction transfer or removability. No capability or benign-prompt check after intervention. Evaluation prompts are excluded from the region means but used in clustering and selection. 32 prompts per layer, judged by a single LLM judge.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, its removal at every layer and position, adding it to induce refusal on harmless prompts, or preservation of general capability.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Tests EP region-mean spans, not affine/cone geometry or a dominant direction plus other directions as such.
Tests EP harmful-region membership against refusal and compliance, not a direct encoding or probe of the model's harmfulness judgment.
Tests region correspondence across Gemma and Llama checkpoints; does not test language transfer or whether the same single direction transfers.
Compares base and instruction-tuned checkpoints, but does not control the training process or establish how training creates or removes a single ablatable direction.

statements.problem: Nothing wrong in the visible parts about this study; its numbers fall in the truncated part. Nuance: the 'projection' control resets the span coordinate to the calibration centre, so it is itself an affine edit with a different reference point.

statements.correction: Tested layers: Gemma L8/L14/L18/L24 = 0.12/0.88/0.22/0.16; Llama L10/L14/L17/L31 = 0.19/0.91/0.16/0.03 (at L31, 30/32 outputs empty). L14 is the highest of the four tested layers; the authors say the full range of effective layers is unknown.
statements.problem: 'Only at L14' is overstated. Only four layers per model were tested, and the authors say they do not know the full range of effective layers. The explicit 0.00 baseline was measured on the L14 run.

statements.correction: 2605.14347: Gemma-2-2B-it and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; prompts from AdvBench/JailbreakBench/MaliciousInstruct/StrongREJECT/HarmBench in chat format, no attack stated; 75/78 (Llama) and 32/34 (Gemma) complied prompts lie in wholly harmful final-token EP regions; 52/91 Llama harmful regions fully refused; unsupervised clustering, correlational.
statements.problem: The study is cited (r15, r16, r19) under harm-under-shift. Its compliant prompts are plain harmful-benchmark prompts with no language, syntax, tool or jailbreak shift. Its numbers are cut off.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B-it L14 harmful-span projection without benign add-back
reader_labels.reason: The span projection left compliance at 0.00, contrary to the expected removal of refusal (r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct L14 harmful-span projection without benign add-back
reader_labels.reason: Projection raised compliance only to 0.34, well below the full-swap result (r10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: L14 region-mean span intervention in the two instruction-tuned models
reader_labels.reason: Full harmful-to-benign region-span swaps raised compliance to 0.88 and 0.91, while harmful-span projection alone was much less effective (r2, r6, r9, r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The swap gave only partial compliance at several layers and Llama L31 generation was mostly empty (r1, r3–r5, r7–r8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Instruction-tuned Gemma and Llama harmful prompts and regions
reader_labels.reason: Compliant prompts largely remained in wholly harmful regions, and only some wholly harmful regions were fully refused, showing that harmful-region membership does not determine refusal (r15–r19).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Wholly harmful regions across the instruction-tuned Gemma and Llama models
reader_labels.reason: Harmful-region round-trip correspondence was 44% across all layer pairs and 68% at selected best-separated layer pairs (r27, r30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: All-region correspondence and aggregate harmful-region transfer
reader_labels.reason: All-region correspondence fell from 34.5% to 32.4%; aggregate harmful-region correspondence after tuning was 44%, not complete transfer (r26–r29).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Base versus instruction-tuned Gemma and Llama checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Instruction-tuned checkpoints showed near-complete harmful-prompt clustering at best-separated layers, while base checkpoints showed substantially lower coverage (r20–r25).
